decisions.target: Passengers booked on Kestrel flights to or from Orlando or Philadelphia between December 21 and December 27

actions.action: Backup ground handling contract at both bases for the strike days
Rebooking deal with a partner airline for 2 disrupted weeks
Free changes and cancellations for bookings in a 2-week window

decisions.message: Kestrel Air update: workers at our ground handling contractor in Orlando and Philadelphia plan a 48-hour strike on Dec 22-23. We have hired a backup ground handling team for both airports, but some flights may still be late or canceled. If you are booked between Dec 14 and Dec 27, you can change or cancel for free in the app now. If your flight is canceled, we will rebook you on Kestrel or a partner airline, or give you a full refund if you prefer. We will text you first if anything changes.
decisions.why:
Own seats in week 8 are 97% booked, so most strike-day passengers can only be protected by moving early or by a partner airline.
The backup contract lowers cancellations on the days that count for goal 2 and insures against an extension that would count for goal 1.
Telling people a week ahead, honestly, is what the CEO says passengers remember.

decisions.target: Passengers booked on Kestrel flights at Orlando or Philadelphia on December 22 or 23

actions.action: Hotel rooms held for stranded passengers, whatever the cause
Extra airport and call-center staff for 2 weeks
Goodwill for affected passengers, up to 10,000 passengers

decisions.message: Kestrel Air: if the Dec 22-23 strike strands you overnight, hotel rooms are held for you, whatever the cause. Extra staff are at our Orlando and Philadelphia airports and on our phone lines. If your flight is canceled or more than 3 hours late, you will also get a $75 Kestrel travel credit.
decisions.why:
The strike days are where complaints and NPS are made.
Hotels and staff on the day stop a delay from becoming a stranding story.
The credit is cheap and mostly used on seats that would fly empty.
